title: Shared definitions
description: Common types for governance records. Draft-07 so a stock python jsonschema validates it with no extra toolchain.

actorId.description: Namespaced actor identity. The prefix is what makes producer!=reviewer checkable.

evidenceTrust.description: HOW MUCH this record's claim is worth, which is a different question from who it names. self_reported: whoever wrote the record asserted it, and nothing checked — any actor that can run repository scripts can produce one, so this is the honest label for a declared intent. deterministic_runner: a program with a fixed output produced it and the run can be repeated. independent_reviewer: a different actor than the producer, in a clean read-only context. authenticated_human: a channel that ISSUES IDENTITY vouched for a person — a GitHub required review, a protected environment. external_policy: an authority outside this repository. WHAT THIS IS NOT: these records are files, and a file is not authenticated by a field inside it. An actor that can write the record can write any value here. The vocabulary makes the claim explicit and checkable for CONSISTENCY; it does not verify it. Anything that must genuinely be authenticated has to arrive from a channel that issues identity, and this harness reads no such channel today.
evidenceTrust.$comment: Ordered weakest to strongest. Do not reorder — validate_governance.py compares by membership, not index, but the guide quotes this order.

provenance.description: How the actor was operating when it produced this record.

cleanContext.description: true = no memory of producing the work under review
